meta.description: Final-year B.Tech CSE (Data Science) student building measured, production-grade systems — agentic RAG, MLOps forecasting, applied ML for support triage, customer analytics, and the full-stack services around them.

hero.name: Goli Pavan Sai Krishna
hero.tagline: Building AI and ML systems end to end — agentic RAG, forecasting, applied ML, and the full-stack services that ship them.

about.heading: About
about.bio: I'm a final-year B.Tech CSE (Data Science) student at NIIT University, building end-to-end AI and ML systems rather than notebooks — an agentic RAG pipeline that audits insurance bills clause-by-clause with zero fabricated citations, a Kubernetes autoscaler that forecasts traffic and beats the stock autoscaler by 62% (and honestly reports where it didn't), a support platform that classifies every incoming complaint and routes it by urgency through an explainable priority engine, a customer analytics pipeline that turns raw transactions into ranked retention decisions, and a hybrid recommender built to replace a feature that turned out to be a hardcoded constant. I care most about systems that measure their own claims instead of asserting them.

projects.name: Bill Auditor
bullets: Audits hospital bills against insurance policy documents line-by-line, citing the exact clause behind every deduction
Zero fabricated clause citations across all recorded evaluation versions
Hybrid dense + lexical retrieval (ChromaDB + BM25) with cross-encoder reranking over a 399-clause index
LLM never performs arithmetic — all money math runs in Python, keeping every figure verifiable
Evaluation harness scores 328 bill lines against a model-derived answer key; accuracy threshold gates CI and blocks regressions
492 unit tests across an 8-stage Jenkins pipeline, deployed to Kubernetes

projects.name: Predictive Autoscaling for Kubernetes

metric.caption: Three runs per arm, identical traffic

bullets: Built an autoscaler that forecasts traffic 60 seconds ahead and adds pods before the load arrives, instead of after
Cut p99 latency 62% (479 → 183 ms) vs default Kubernetes autoscaling — three runs per arm on byte-identical traffic, for 28% more compute
Forecast request rate with a LightGBM quantile model on 39 time-series features, tuned to over-predict since running short costs 10x more
Fixed a 40% slowdown on traffic spikes by raising the HPA's floor instead of setting pods directly — 49% better than HPA alone
Safety checks declined to act on 23% of 980 logged decisions where the forecast wasn't trustworthy

projects.name: Complaint Classification & Resolution System

metric.caption: 78.8% exact, 0.79 macro-F1 on a held-out set

projects.description: A support platform where an AI pipeline reads every incoming complaint the moment it arrives — category, sentiment, urgency and a draft reply — so agents work a prioritised queue instead of a first-in-first-out inbox.
bullets: An urgent case — fraud, a refund never received, a legal threat — surfaces at the top of the queue instead of waiting behind routine complaints
TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier reaches 78.8% accuracy and 0.79 macro-F1 on a held-out test set, tuned by 5-fold grid search
Returns its own confidence with every prediction and routes low-confidence complaints to human review rather than trusting a shaky guess
De-duplicating the dataset before training caught 4 complaints leaking across train and test and 3 carrying contradictory labels
Pretrained DistilBERT supplies three-class sentiment; a transparent rules engine combines category, sentiment and an urgent-keyword list into Low, Medium, High or Urgent
Gemini drafts a suggested reply grounded in the complaint's own text and classification — always reviewed and edited by an agent, never sent to a customer by the model
Three independently deployable services with 227 tests across four suites, containerised with Docker and deployed to Kubernetes by a Jenkins pipeline

projects.name: Customer Segmentation & Retention
bullets: Processes 540K+ raw transactions into 391K validated records across 4,334 customers
Crosses BG/NBD + Gamma-Gamma lifetime value with XGBoost churn risk (0.78 ROC-AUC) into an action matrix
Flagged 229 high-value, high-risk customers worth £16.5K in predicted 90-day revenue
RFM features with K-Means segments give each customer a readable label, not an opaque score
MLflow experiment tracking and DVC data versioning, served via FastAPI backend and React dashboard

projects.name: MSME Marketplace — Recommendation Engine & Code Audit

metric.caption: From zero coverage to three suites

projects.description: An e-commerce platform for small Indian manufacturers. I inherited a four-person codebase, audited it end to end, and replaced a fabricated recommendation feature with a real one.
bullets: Built a hybrid recommendation service as its own FastAPI process — TF-IDF content similarity blended 0.6/0.4 with co-purchase collaborative filtering, with explicit cold-start handling
Replaced a feature advertised in the UI as “XGBoost-driven forecasting” that was in fact a hardcoded constant
Audited the inherited codebase end to end and fixed the access-control and data-exposure bugs it surfaced, including a path that let any logged-in user escalate their own role
Rebuilt authentication on httpOnly cookies with 15-minute access tokens and refresh-token rotation
Took the project from zero tests to 133 across three suites — Jest, pytest and Playwright
Containerised all three services as non-root images and deployed them on AWS k3s with automatic TLS for about $23/month

projects.name: MSME Marketplace — Security Audit & Recommendation Engine

metric.caption: Auth and access control, documented and fixed

projects.description: An e-commerce platform for small Indian manufacturers. I audited the codebase end to end, fixed the security holes I found, and built a real recommendation service in place of a fabricated one.
bullets: Audited the full codebase and documented 11 auth and access-control weaknesses, including a privilege escalation that let any logged-in user make themselves an administrator
Found and removed a line disabling TLS certificate verification for the entire Node process, and fixed two endpoints leaking other customers' names, phone numbers and shipping addresses
Moved auth from JWT in localStorage to httpOnly cookies with 15-minute access tokens, refresh-token rotation with replay detection, and CSRF protection

Found a feature advertised as "XGBoost-driven forecasting" that was a hardcoded constant, removed the false claim, and built a real hybrid recommender — TF-IDF content similarity blended 0.6/0.4 with co-purchase collaborative filtering, evaluated on a time-based split
Took the project from zero tests to 133 across three suites, and deployed all three services to AWS on k3s with Let's Encrypt TLS and a Jenkins pipeline
